# mabinogi-007 — review

## Pass 1 (units)

Reviewer pass 1 (2026-11-13). I read all 81 units and the "about" against conventions.md, packet.md (the established text and the establishment log), the published mabinogi-004, 005 and 006, and drafts/mabinogi-006/review.md. Aids: Strachan, Morris-Jones, Silvan Evans and GPC, from knowledge. Third witness: Rhŷs & Evans 1905 (Red Book), `source/raw/rhys-evans1905_djvu.txt`, printed pp. 39–43 (the OCR, read with its usual misreadings of 6, ƒ and r-rotunda). No English translation was consulted. Edits were made by a Python script (load, change fields by index, dump with ensure_ascii=False, indent=1). No `t` was touched. Afterwards I checked that there are 81 sentences and that every `t` equals cut.json.

**Unit numbers are 0-based.**

### Changes

- 2 · l, i, n · major · Name forms did not match the published parts. The draft had "Nysien" (005 has Nisien throughout) and "Eurosswydd" (005 has Euroswydd in l and i). · l and i now read "Nisien son of Euroswydd". The note says Nyssyen is Nisien "as the earlier parts write the name" and explains the ss. The closing list of uncles now reads "Nisien".
- 33 · l, i, n · major · *Tal Ebolyon* was "Talybolion" in l and i. 005 (unit 101) writes "Tal Ebolion" in l and i, and its note gives the manuscript's *Tal Ebolyon*. · l and i now read "in Tal Ebolion". The note says Tal Ebolyon is Tal Ebolion and points to its explanation in 005. (The brief said "Tal Ebolyon". The published English form is Tal Ebolion, and I followed the published part.)
- 7 · i, n · minor · i "I swear to God" is a stock English oath, not built from *Y Duw y dygaf uyg kyffes*. 004 renders *ym kyffes y Duw* as "by my confession to God". i also lost the *a gyflauan* "an … outrage" construction. The note did not say what softens *gyflauan* or *wneuthur*. · i now reads "“To God I make my confession,” he said in his heart, “the household would think it an unlikely outrage, the one I am going to do this very hour.”" The note now names the causes: *kyflauan* is softened after *a*, with the same adjective + *a* + noun shape as *Da a dwy ynys* in unit 36, and *gwneuthur* is softened after *y* 'to'. It also cross-refers to 004's oath. The construction is still marked uncertain.
- 8 · l, i, n · minor · i "before any man in the house could lay hold on him" follows the Red Book's *kynn kael* 'before … got'. The White Book has *na chael*, still governed by *heb*: 'without any man getting'. l "into the fire" also hid *kynneu* 'kindling'. · i now reads "with no man in the house able to lay hold on him". l reads "into the kindling". The note now says *na chael* is still under *heb* and gives the Red Book's *kynn kael*.
- 63 · l, i, n · minor · The note called "The Hospitality of the Noble Head" "the conventional English", which means the phrase was remembered rather than built. · Rebuilt from GPC *urddol* 'honoured, dignified'. l now reads "the Hospitality of-the-Honoured Head" and i "the Hospitality of the Honoured Head". The "conventional English" sentence is gone. The note now glosses *urdaul* 'honoured, dignified' (*urddol*, from *urdd*). The point that the sense of *yspydawt* is disputed stays.
- 80 · n · minor · Two problems. *y ginyaw* was called "softened, as in the Red Book" with no cause given; *kinyaw* is normally masculine, so softening after the article needs a comment (the drafter flagged this). The Red Book reading was also misquoted as *deg wlat* 'ten lands' alone. · The note now says *y ginyaw* is softened after the article as if feminine, though the word is usually masculine, and that the Red Book agrees. It now gives the full Red Book reading, *deg wlat a seith ugeint*, 150. (006's review gives 144 for the Red Book's earlier count; the two counts in the Red Book differ.)
- 0 · n · style · *daruot* was called "the verbal noun of darfu". *darfu* is the preterite, not a lemma. · Now "(modern darfod), the verbal noun whose preterite is daruu (darfu)".
- 5 · i · style · "Let him go, and welcome" adds a flavour of permission. *yn llawen* qualifies the going, and the next unit repeats it as narrative (*a aeth attaw yn llawen*). · i now reads "Let him go gladly", which keeps the echo.
- 12 · n · style · "not mutated since g is its first letter and the word is masculine" muddled the reason. · Now: unchanged after the article because it is masculine (a feminine noun would lose its g).
- 13 · i · style · "cried … !" gave more force than *y dywot* 'said' and the text's full stop. · i now reads "said, … Tyllion.”" The cry itself is still left untranslated.
- 14 · n · style · The note did not say which *y* stands before *taryan*. l has "the shield" and i has "his shield". · The note now says that softening is expected whether *y* is 'his' or the article, because *tarian* is feminine.
- 43 · i · style · "they asked": the house i for *heb* + pronoun is "said", and 005 has “What is that?” they said. · i now reads "they said".
- 45 · n · style · The note did not give the cause of the softening in *wiscaw*. · Added: softened as the subject of *daroed*.
- 47 · n · style · The note did not give the cause of the softening in *y gallon*. · Added: *calon* softened after *y* 'his'.
- 57 · n · style · *Weldy* was called "softened" with no cause, and *dylywn* was given no tense. · *Weldy*: the g is lost, as in *wele* 'behold'. *dylywn*: 1 pl. imperfect, the tense this verb uses for 'ought'.
- 60 · l · style · *dwyn yspeit* was "spending a-while" in l, but the note glosses *dwyn* 'carry, bear', and 006's l uses "bore" for *duc*. · l now reads "bearing a-while".
- 76 · l · style · *lau heb lau* was "hand by hand" in l, but the note glosses it 'hand past hand'. · l now reads "hand past hand".

### Establishment-log items: all stated plainly
- Opening mid-line in col. 55, no initial (0). The space before *urenhin* is layout (4). The scribe's blank in *tranoeth [ ] y bore* (16).
- *Guern gwngwch uiwch*: Evans's division, the witness's *gwn, gwchuiwch* and the Red Book's *g6ng6ch ui6ch* are given, and the cry is marked obscure (13).
- *guae ni*: kept, with the Red Book's and the witness's *ui*. The note says *ni* does not sit with *o'm* (36).
- *y glan Alaw* = *yg* + nasal-mutated *glan*. The division is ours, following 006's *y gwaelawt* (38).
- *o uwyt*: the raised *u* (49). *[gyt ac]* is in the witness, not in Evans or the Red Book, and is not supplied (50).
- *Ac ar hynny o gin—*: the false start at the leaf end, said not to be a catchword, with the Red Book having it once (52).
- *yneuad* as one word (55). *y mywn* (73).
- *Yspydawt Uranwen a Matholwch …* is running text in Evans. The witness's braces and the Red Book are given, and i has brackets (64).
- *kychu*: certain on the image, with the witness's *kyrchu* and the Red Book's *kychwynnu*. Marked uncertain (68).
- *ac ar Yspydaut*: kept, with the witness's *am* and the Red Book's *ar* (80).
- *Pendarar*: the note says the text has -r (and the Red Book too). l and i have "Pendaran Dyfed", as in 004 and 006 (48).
- No words supplied, and no note says otherwise.

### Drafter's flags, verified
- 10 / 14 *a'y tarean*, *y taryan*: unsoftened, rightly called so. After 'y 'his' one expects *darean*, and after the article or 'his' one expects *daryan* (*tarian* is feminine). The Red Book also has *ae taryan* at 10 but *y daryan* at 14, and the note says both. Kept, with the clarification above.
- 47 *a torres*: in this spelling a softened t is written d, so this is unsoftened after the relative. The Red Book also has *a tozres* [= torres]. The claim is right.
- 20 *Emystynnu idaw ynteu*: *y* 'to' marking the agent of an intransitive verbal noun is right, as in modern *wedi iddo …*. The Red Book has *Ymestynnu ida6 ynteu*. The note stands.
- 40 *bydant* as habitual present 3 pl. (the Red Book also has *ybydant*), and 52 / 69 *bydynt* as habitual past (imperfect) 3 pl. Both labels are right.
- 51 *y guelet* = *eu gwelet* 'their seeing'. The Red Book writes *eu g6elet*, and *eu* does not mutate. Right.
- 59 *ouut* = *gofut* softened after *o* (g lost), 'grief'. Right. The Red Book's word here is garbled in the OCR, so it is not cited.
- 80 *y ginyaw*: corrected (above).
- 7 *a gyflauan … y wneuthur*: hedged, and the causes are now added (above). The Red Book has the same words.
- 8 *y gynneu* after *y*: the note's "not clear" is honest. *kynneu* is a verbal noun and would not normally soften after the article; the Red Book's *yn y gynneu tan* shows the same form. Left as stated.
- 17 *heb enni*: the two readings (*genni* 'have room' and *geni* 'be born', the Red Book's *eni*) are both stated, and it is marked uncertain. Kept.

### Considered and refused
- 70 / 79 "Fortunate Concealment", "Unfortunate Disclosure", "Unfortunate Blow": this is the plain sense of the parts (*mat* 'good, fortunate' + *cud* 'hiding'; *anfad* + *datcud* 'uncovering'; *anfad* + *palfawd*), not a borrowed phrase. The note already says *mat* / *anuat* are disputed. Kept.
- 17 i "had no place anywhere": this commits to the *genni* reading. Any i must choose, and the note gives both. Kept.
- 9 i "between her two brothers": "her" is fair English for *y deu uroder*, and the note identifies the two. Kept.
- 20 i "and his own heart burst with it": "with it" is a slight addition but carries the *yny … ac yny* sequence. Kept.
- 26 / 53 / 80 *kinyaw* "dinner" in l and "feast" in i: this is consistent across the part. Kept.
- 65 i "spoke up" for *Sef a wnaeth*: *Sef* is dropped by house rule, and "spoke up" is what he did. Kept.
- 75 l "were-reared" for active *a uagyssant*: the note states the construction is loose and offers both readings. Kept.
- 7 / 17 i "in his heart" for *yn y uedwl* 'in his mind': idiomatic, and l keeps "mind". Kept.
- 62 *gyduot*: the cause of the softening is unstated, but the Red Book's *gytuot* is given. Not worth a change.
- 23 the witness's *Gliuieu. eil taran* division and 13 the witness's misplaced quote are punctuation decisions already recorded in the log. They need no note.
- about: the names agree with the published parts (Efnysien, Caswallon, Gwales, Penfro), and no name fixed above appears in it. Unchanged.
